answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond on the sable ledger, files one yarrow record, and pays a burned fee. The prism board publishes confirmed fakes; the fee starts at 40 credits and rises 40 per 100 confirmed fakes. With 900 confirmed fakes, the 1,000th fake costs 400, and 1,000 fakes cost 220,000 in fees. Auditors sample 10% and publish the count for recomputation. A rented-filing ring fails: filings are key-bound, so a rented record's owner key shows as a duplicate and the bond burns. An honest identity pays 40 once, recovering its 60 bond after a clean epoch.
